start_with: Confirm the page uses a Lava Application Content block or otherwise loads HTMX.

Confirm `hx-target` matches an existing element at request time.
Walk up the DOM and inspect inherited HTMX attributes.
Inspect the network response and returned fragment.

Confirm the client actually sent a body and inspect its content type.
Use `Body` when object conversion is expected and `RawBody` when the original string is required.

Determine whether the installation uses core Rock 18+ assets or the Helix plugin.
Test the appropriate asset path directly.

start_with: Inspect the endpoint for `{% javascript %}` or `{% stylesheet %}`.
Remove the assumption that those commands can register assets from a Helix fragment.
Move the dependency to a verified page, theme, or block-level loading boundary.
Retest both the initial render and later fragment replacements.
Stop when the dependency is loaded once through a supported host and the fragment works without endpoint-side resource registration.

Compare total execution time and database activity across representative requests.
Inspect repeated or unexpectedly expensive database calls.
Use targeted query diagnostics only for a bounded investigation and review whether parameters contain personal data.
Retest after each change.

start_with: Confirm whether state exists only in browser-side variables.

Include those values in filter and refresh requests.
Have sortable headers send the next sort and direction explicitly.
Define ordering for null or blank values.
Retest filtering, sorting, manual refresh, and auto-refresh together.
